figures.finding: An employee's monthly pay is taxed at 0% to SCR 8,555.50 for a citizen (15% for a non-citizen), 15% to 10,000, 20% to 83,333 and 30% above; a sole trader's business income above SCR 1 million turnover is taxed at 0% on the first SCR 102,666, 15% to 1 million and 25% above, and below SCR 1 million turnover a presumptive 1.5% of turnover applies.
figures.applies: Employee rates effective 1 June 2018, still published by SRC in November 2026.

sources.said: BRACKET GROSS MONTHLY INCOME (SCR) RATES FROM TO CITIZEN NON-CITIZEN Bracket 1 SCR 0 SCR 8,555.50 0% 15% Bracket 2 SCR 8,555.51 SCR 10,000.00 15% of the amount in excess of SCR 8,555.50 15% of the amount not exceeding SCR 10,000.00 Bracket 3 SCR 10,000.01 SCR 83,333.00 SCR 216 plus 20% of the amount in excess of SCR 10,000.00 SCR 1,500 plus 20% of the amount in excess of SCR 10,000.00 Bracket 4 > 83,333 SCR 14,883.28 + 30% of the amount in excess of SCR 83,333.00
Sole Trader and Partnership 0% on the first SCR 102, 666.‎ ‎15% between SCR 102,666.01 up to SCR 1 million.‎ 25% above SCR 1 million.
for small businesses with an annual turnover below SCR 1 million. Tax Rate Applicable at a flat rate of 1.5% on the annual business turnover

figures.finding: The tax year is the calendar year; a business tax return is due by 31 March after it.
figures.applies: Business taxpayers; employees are taxed by monthly withholding.

sources.said: All business tax return must be submitted to SRC no later than 31 March of every tax year,

figures.finding: The employer withholds income tax from emoluments monthly and pays it to SRC within 21 days of the following month.

sources.said: Income tax is usually withheld on the emoluments of employees by the employer and is remitted to the Seychelles Revenue Commission (SRC) on a monthly basis using the Business Activity Statement (BAS).
Pay the tax withheld to SRC within 21 days of the following applicable month using the BAS.

figures.finding: A promoter or agent paying a non-resident entertainer for a performance in Seychelles withholds 5%, final; royalties to a non-resident bear 15%.

sources.said: In respect of a promoter, agent, or similar person paying ‎remuneration to a non-resident entertainer or sports person in ‎respect of a performance or sporting event in Seychelles.‎ ‎5%
Dividend, interest, royalty, natural resource amount, or technical ‎services fee paid to a non-resident.‎ 15%
As withholding tax is a final tax

figures.finding: VAT is 15% on most supplies (0% on exports); a person must register once taxable supplies reach SCR 2,000,000 in 12 months and may register voluntarily from SCR 100,000 (from 1 January 2025).

sources.said: The 15% standard rate applied on most imported goods or services sold in Seychelles.

shall come into operation on the 1st January, 2025. … Registration threshold (a) The registration threshold for the purposes of section 7 is SCR2,000,000. (b) The registration threshold for the purposes of section 9 of the Value Added Tax Act is SCR100,000.

figures.finding: An employee pays 5% of pay to the Seychelles Pension Fund and the employer 5%, and a self-employed worker 10%, from 1 January 2023 (still in force in 2026; a three-month deferral of the employer share in 2026 covered only tourism, wholesale and retail employers).

sources.said: mandatory contribution rates will be increased effective 1st of January, 2023; as follows: For employees, the increase in contribution rate will be from 4% to 5% For employers, the contribution rate will remain at 5%. Pension contribution for self-employed will increase from 9% to 10%.

SPF shall introduce a deferred contribution option for employers only, for a period of 3 months, starting from March 2026 contributions due on 21st April 2026 until May 2026. … The proposal shall be applicable to all employers within the tourism industry, wholesaler and retail businesses only
